selected_experiment.question: Within new substitution-argument events whose argument object was generated by substitute, is the remaining cross-product driven by a small hot basis of expression identities, a small hot basis of argument identities, or diffuse on both sides?
selected_experiment.scope: newArgument events only, argument provenance exactly substitute

classification_rule.hot_expression_basis: top-32 expression identities cover >= 80% of scoped events in both cases
classification_rule.hot_argument_basis: top-32 argument identities cover >= 80% of scoped events in both cases

post_result_policy.if_hot_expression_basis: prospectively test a compiled substitution plan per hot expression, with exact argument/depth inputs and no cross-argument result reuse
post_result_policy.if_hot_argument_basis: inspect whether existing shift/transport compilation already captures the dominant argument side before adding another cache
post_result_policy.if_bilateral_hot_basis: test the cheaper of expression-plan compilation and argument-side transport compilation prospectively
post_result_policy.if_diffuse_cross_product: compile obstruction against identity-local caching and move to a higher-level substitution representation
post_result_policy.if_one_sided: target only the hot side and retain the diffuse side as protected distinction

claim_boundary: Diagnostic identity fanout only. Object identities are runtime-local; concentration licenses a prospective representation experiment, not semantic equivalence between distinct expressions or arguments.
